title: Derived mapping modules in one directed enriched amalgamation
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and derived enriched coends in chronological order of [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda]. All data are small in a fixed universe. Let $L,O,R$ be disjoint sets. Let $A,B,T$ be simplicial categories with object sets $L\amalg O$, $O\amalg R$, and $O$, respectively. Let $T\to A$ and $T\to B$ be enriched functors equal to the indicated inclusion on objects, inducing weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping sets between objects of $O$. Assume $A(o,l)=\varnothing$ and $B(r,o)=\varnothing$ for $l\in L,o\in O,r\in R$. Let $Z$ be a homotopy pushout of $A\leftarrow T\to B$ in the Bergner model structure; its objects may be taken to be $L\amalg O\amalg R$. Here a homotopy pushout means the ordinary colimit of a cofibrant replacement of the span, up to Dwyer--Kan equivalence, with its cocone maps.

The cocone maps from $A$ and $B$ are weak homotopy equivalences on their mapping sets, and $Z(r,l)$ is empty up to weak homotopy equivalence. The new mapping spaces are naturally
$$Z(l,r)\simeq A(l,-)|_T\otimes_T^{\mathbb L}B(-,r)|_T.$$
The comparison to $Z(l,r)$ is the derived composition pairing of its two cocone maps. The assertions are natural for maps of such spans preserving the three blocks, including arbitrary enriched maps on the blocks, and retain the $A|_L^{\mathrm{op}}\times B|_R$ module variables. Empty blocks and empty mapping sets are allowed; no local Kan hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Appendix A.3.2 (enriched model structures) and A.3.3 (enriched diagram model structures), background only. Agent-formulated auxiliary assertion for one directed gluing along a homotopically full middle block; not a quoted theorem of HTT. Archival source WANTED. proof.text: First make the middle block strictly full. Define $A_0$ with the same objects and mapping sets as $A$ except that its $O$-by-$O$ mapping sets are those of $T$. Composition inside $O$ is that of $T$, and composition on $A(l,o)$ uses the given $T$-action; all other compositions are inherited from $A$. There is no composition $O\to L\to O$, because $A(o,l)$ is empty, so these prescriptions are associative and exhaustive. Define $B_0$ in the same way using $B(r,o)=\varnothing$. The functors $A_0\to A$ and $B_0\to B$ fix objects and are weak equivalences on mapping sets: only the middle mapping sets change, and there the assertion is a hypothesis. Thus they are Dwyer--Kan equivalences by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The span $A_0\leftarrow T\to B_0$ has genuinely full inclusions.

proof.text: Choose object-preserving local trivial fibrations $S\to T$, $C_L\to A|_L$, and $C_R\to B|_R$ with Bergner-cofibrant sources. They are fixed-object cofibrant replacements; [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] identifies fixed-object cofibrant objects with Bergner-cofibrant ones. Apply [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution] to $A_0$ with diagonal resolutions $(C_L,S)$ and to $B_0$ with $(S,C_R)$. Denote the resulting categories by $\widetilde A,\widetilde B$. Their common full middle subcategory is exactly $S$; both inclusions of $S$ are cofibrations, and all three categories are cofibrant. Their maps to $A_0,T,B_0$ fix objects and are local trivial fibrations. Consequently $P=\widetilde A\amalg_S\widetilde B$ is a representative of the derived pushout by [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Combining these maps of spans with Step 1 identifies its cocone with that of $Z$ in the derived sense. No padding of missing outer objects in a fixed-object span, or single-arrow pushout comparison, is used.

proof.text: Compute this ordinary pushout directly. Put $X_l(s)=\widetilde A(l,s)$ and $Y_r(s)=\widetilde B(s,r)$. Construct a category $P_0$ on $L\amalg O\amalg R$ that agrees with $\widetilde A,\widetilde B$ on their pairs, has $P_0(r,l)=\varnothing$, and has $P_0(l,r)=X_l\otimes_S Y_r$. This is the coequalizer of [def-coef-enriched-coend], with its two factors interchanged to chronological order. Its relations identify $(xf,y)$ with $(x,fy)$. The composite of $x:l\to s$ and $y:s\to r$ is their coend class. Composition at the endpoints is induced from composition in $\widetilde A,\widetilde B$; the displayed balancing relation and the associativity and commuting module-action identities make these operations well defined and associative. These are all possible compositions, since no arrow decreases the block label. A pair of functors from $\widetilde A,\widetilde B$ agreeing on $S$ extends uniquely to $P_0$: on $(x,y)$ it must take the composite of their images, and this is balanced over $S$. Conversely every functor from $P_0$ restricts to that pair. Restriction and extension are inverse, also with any prescribed object function. This proves the ordinary pushout universal property, so $P=P_0$, including its cocone maps.

source.place: Inherited auxiliary directed-gluing branch; agent proof, not an assertion quoted from the current coefficient-limit proof

proof.text: For fixed $l,r$, the lemma [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution] makes $X_l$ projectively cofibrant over $S$ and $Y_r$ projectively cofibrant over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence their ordinary coend already computes the derived coend as defined in [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda]. More explicitly, take projective cofibrant replacements of either module. The invariance clauses of [lem-coef-enriched-coend-homotopy-invariance], first with the other module fixed and then with its replacement fixed, show that the two replacement augmentations induce weak equivalences on coends. Step 3 therefore gives $P(l,r)\simeq X_l\otimes_S^{\mathbb L}Y_r$, through its composition augmentation.

source.place: Inherited auxiliary directed-gluing branch; agent proof, not an assertion quoted from the current coefficient-limit proof

proof.text:
Compare the bar for $(X_l,S,Y_r)$ with the bar for $(A(l,-)|_T,T,B(-,r)|_T)$ using the resolution maps. In degree $n$ this is the coproduct over the same tuples $(o_0,\ldots,o_n)$ of the maps
$$X_l(o_0)\times S(o_0,o_1)\times\cdots\times S(o_{n-1},o_n)\times Y_r(o_n)\longrightarrow A(l,o_0)\times T(o_0,o_1)\times\cdots\times T(o_{n-1},o_n)\times B(o_n,r).$$
Every factor is a trivial Kan fibration by Step 2 and [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution]. The boundary lifting criterion of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] shows that their finite product is a trivial fibration by lifting each coordinate. Their coproduct is also a trivial fibration: a simplex of the target belongs to one summand, whose index is forced on the lifting problem, and one lifts in that summand (including the empty-boundary case). Thus the comparison is a weak equivalence in every bar degree. Homotopy realization preserves this degreewise weak equivalence, by definition of a derived realization; concretely, [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] also gives a weak equivalence of the bar diagonals. The two-sided bar formula of [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda] identifies their homotopy realizations with the derived coends, proving
$$P(l,r)\simeq A(l,-)|_T\otimes_T^{\mathbb L}B(-,r)|_T.$$

proof.text: For pairs in the $A$-side, Step 3 gives $P(a,a')=\widetilde A(a,a')$, and on the $B$-side it gives $P(b,b')=\widetilde B(b,b')$. The two prescriptions agree on the common full $S$-block. Their resolution maps are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution], and the maps $A_0\to A,B_0\to B$ of Step 1 are weak equivalences on mapping sets. Hence the derived cocone maps from $A,B$ are weak equivalences on their own mapping spaces. Also $P(r,l)=\varnothing$ exactly. Object-preserving local weak equivalences are Dwyer--Kan equivalences by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], so these conclusions give the asserted statements for a homotopy-pushout representative $Z$ at the corresponding cocone objects.

source.place: Inherited auxiliary directed-gluing branch; agent proof, not an assertion quoted from the current coefficient-limit proof

proof.text: Check the specified comparison and naturality. The map from each bar summand to the pushout composes its successive arrows; a face composes adjacent arrows or applies an action, and a degeneracy inserts an identity. Thus its augmentation is precisely the derived composition pairing of the two cocone maps. A block-preserving map of spans sends each summand to the summand with the image tuple and applies the given functor to every factor. It preserves all these compositions, actions and identities, even when it identifies objects in a block. The functorial resolutions of [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution] and the natural derived-pushout comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping] give the same map on the two sides of Step 5. Composition at the endpoints acts on the first and last factors. The additional-variable and augmentation clauses of [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda] preserve these actions. Initially they are actions by $C_L^{\mathrm{op}}\times C_R$; restriction along its object-preserving Dwyer--Kan equivalence to $A|_L^{\mathrm{op}}\times B|_R$ is a Quillen equivalence on modules by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], so the comparison retains the stated original module variables. If $O$ is empty the coend and every bar degree are empty; if an outer block is empty there is no corresponding mixed pair. Empty mapping factors give empty summands. All arguments use cofibrant resolutions and homotopy realization, so no local Kan hypothesis was introduced.
